```{r}

# Load packages
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Import your DHS PR file
pr <- read_dta("D:/My Document Classes/RWPR81FL.DTA")

# Examine the data
glimpse(pr)
names(pr)
```
```{r}
# Prepare the variables for plotting
pr_clean <- pr %>%
  mutate(
    age = if_else(hv105 <= 97, as.numeric(hv105), NA_real_),

    sex = factor(
      as.numeric(hv104),
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),

    residence = factor(
      as.numeric(hv025),
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("Urban", "Rural")
    ),

    wealth = factor(
      as.numeric(hv270),
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c("Poorest", "Poorer", "Middle",
                 "Richer", "Richest")
    ),

    education = factor(
      as.numeric(hv106),
      levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3),
      labels = c("No education", "Primary",
                 "Secondary", "Higher")
    ),

    years_schooling = if_else(
      hv108 <= 90,
      as.numeric(hv108),
      NA_real_
    ),

    weight = as.numeric(hv005) / 1000000
  )
```
```{r}
# geom_bar() — Bar chart
# geom_bar() automatically counts the observations in each category
# Objective: Show the number of household members by sex.

pr_clean %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sex, fill = sex)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Geom_Bar of Household Members by Sex",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Number of Members"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# geom_boxplot()/Box plot
# for Comparing the distribution of age between urban and rural residents.
# A box plot displays the median, quartiles, and potential outliers.
pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = residence, y = age,
             fill = residence)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Geom_boxplot of Age Distribution by Residence",
    x = "Residence",
    y = "Age in Years"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
#geom_density() — Density plot to show smooth representation of a numerical//
#variable's distribution
#Compare age distributions between males and females


pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age, fill = sex,
             color = sex)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Density by Sex",
    x = "Age in Years",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# geom_histogram() — Histogram to examine the shape of age distribution of 
# household members.
pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 5,     # 5 age groups into intervals of five years
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Geom_histogram of Age Distribution of Household Members",
    x = "Age in Years",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# geom_hline() /Horizontal reference line
# Show mean years of schooling by wealth quintile, with a horizontal line representing the overall average.

school_data <- pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(years_schooling), !is.na(wealth))

school_summary <- school_data %>%
  group_by(wealth) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_years = mean(years_schooling),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

overall_mean <- mean(school_data$years_schooling)

ggplot(school_summary,
       aes(x = wealth, y = mean_years)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = overall_mean,
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Mean Years of Schooling by Wealth Quintile",
    x = "Wealth Quintile",
    y = "Mean Years of Schooling"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# Geom_jitter()/ Jitter plot for testing relationship btn age and years of schooling

pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age),
         !is.na(years_schooling)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = years_schooling)) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.3,
    height = 0.2,
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = "steelblue"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Jitter plot of Age and Years of Schooling",
    x = "Age in Years",
    y = "Years of Schooling"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# Geom_line()/Line graph to show the # of HH members by single year of age
# It shows how the number of members changes across ages, not over calendar time.

age_summary <- pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  count(age)

ggplot(age_summary, aes(x = age, y = n)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Line graph of Household Members by Age",
    x = "Age in Years",
    y = "Number of Members"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# Geom_point()/Scatter plot to displays individual observations as points.
# The graph examines the  linear relationship between age and years of schooling.

pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age),
         !is.na(years_schooling)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = years_schooling)) +
  geom_point(
    color = "darkgreen",
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Scattet Plot of Age and Years of Schooling",
    x = "Age in Years",
    y = "Years of Schooling"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# Geom_rug()/Rug plot
# It Shows the distribution of ages using small marks along the horizontal axis.

pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age)) +
  geom_density(
    fill = "lightblue",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_rug(
  alpha = 0.05
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Rug Plot of Age Distribution with Rug Plot",
    x = "Age in Years",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
#Geom_smooth()/Smoothed trend
 # To examine the general relationship between age and years of schooling.

pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age),
         !is.na(years_schooling)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = years_schooling)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",   # to add a fitted linear regression line
    color = "red"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Smooth Plot of Relationship Between Age and Schooling",
    x = "Age in Years",
    y = "Years of Schooling"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# Geom_text() /Add data labels 
# Display the number of household members by residence with labels above the bars.

residence_summary <- pr_clean %>%
  count(residence)

ggplot(residence_summary,
       aes(x = residence, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n),
    vjust = -.5,
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Household Members by Residence",
    x = "Residence",
    y = "Number of Members"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}

# Geom_violin()/ Violin plot displays the shape of the distribution.
# Wider sections indicates greater estimated concentration of observations.
 # It compare the distribution of years of schooling by sex.
pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(years_schooling)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sex,
             y = years_schooling,
             fill = sex)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.1,
    fill = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Violin of Years of Schooling by Sex",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Years of Schooling"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# Geom_vline()/Vertical reference line
# Display the age distribution and mark the median age.
# he red vertical line identifies the unweighted median age.

age_data <- pr_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age))

median_age <- median(age_data$age)

ggplot(age_data, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 5,
    fill = "skyblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = median_age,
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Vline of Age Distribution with Median Age",
    x = "Age in Years",
    y = "Number of Members"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
